title: Kamphaeng Phet & Sukhothai 3-Day World Heritage Trip 2026 | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day Kamphaeng Phet to Sukhothai itinerary covering two UNESCO World Heritage cities in Thailand. Cycle the ruins, see Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Chang Rop, Wat Mahathat and Wat Si Chum, with real food stops and checked hours and fees.
keywords: Kamphaeng Phet travel, Sukhothai travel, World Heritage trip Thailand, Sukhothai Historical Park, 3-day itinerary Thailand
h1:
Kamphaeng Phet & Sukhothai
3-Day World Heritage Trip
intro: Two UNESCO World Heritage cities sit barely an hour apart. It's about 77 km by car from Kamphaeng Phet to Sukhothai, so it's easy to fold them into a single trip. This 3-day plan starts at Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park, which most people skip, then moves on to Sukhothai, the old capital where you can spend a whole day cycling between temples. We checked the opening hours and entry fees here against the Fine Arts Department and the park's official pages.

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet and Sukhothai were inscribed as World Heritage together in 1991, under the name "Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns." Most people only know Sukhothai and just drive straight past Kamphaeng Phet, even though Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park is quieter, shadier, and has temples every bit as beautiful. So this trip makes Kamphaeng Phet the star of day one, then closes out in Sukhothai.

This plan assumes you're self-driving, because many of the ruins are spread out beyond the old city wall where public transport doesn't reach. If you don't have a car, renting one or hiring a car with a driver by the day works just as well. The main route is Kamphaeng Phet → Highway 101 through Phran Kratai and Khiri Mat → Old Sukhothai, about 1 hour 15 minutes of driving.

items: Day 1 — Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park, inner-city zone (Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Phra That) plus the Aranyik forest zone (Wat Chang Rop, Wat Phra Si Iriyabot). Overnight in Kamphaeng Phet.

Day 2 — Drive to Sukhothai in the morning, drop your bags at a place near the old town, then cycle the historical park's walled zone in the afternoon (Wat Mahathat, Wat Si Sawai, Wat Sa Si) and catch the sunset. Overnight in the old town.
Day 3 — Morning run to Wat Si Chum and any spots you missed, grab a bowl of original Sukhothai noodles, then head home.

blocks.title: What to know about entry fees
blocks.html: Both historical parks charge entry by zone. Kamphaeng Phet is around 10 THB/zone for Thais and 30 THB for foreigners, open 08:30–16:30. Sukhothai is around 20 THB/zone for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners, opening early from about 06:30 and closing in the evening. Bike rental at the park gate runs 20–30 THB for the whole day. Prices can change, so double-check on site.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Kamphaeng Phet, the city people usually drive past

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park splits into two parts: the walled inner-city zone centered on Wat Phra Kaeo, and the Aranyik zone north of the city, an open forest on a low laterite ridge. The temples in the Aranyik zone are large and shady, so walking under the trees beats baking in the sun. Start the inner-city zone in the morning, then do the Aranyik zone in the late afternoon as the light starts to slant.

items.activity: Start at Wat Phra Kaeo in the heart of the old city
items.note: The city's royal temple, with a lion-base chedi and a large Buddha image now reduced to its core frame — the defining image of Kamphaeng Phet.

items.activity: Walk on to Wat Phra That and the Kamphaeng Phet National Museum
items.note: The museum is nearby — drop in to see Buddha images and ceramics excavated in the area before you go look at the real thing.
Try Kamphaeng Phet chicken noodles or a local curry-and-rice shop to fuel up before tackling the Aranyik zone.

items.activity: Drive into the Aranyik zone, starting at Wat Phra Si Iriyabot
items.note: The highlight is the four-gabled mondop housing Buddha images in four postures — walking, standing, sitting, reclining. The standing figure still shows a clear outline.

items.activity: On to Wat Chang Rop on the highest mound in the Aranyik zone
items.note: A bell-shaped chedi on a square base, originally ringed by 68 stucco elephants around the platform. You can walk up for a view all around.

items.activity: Catch the late-afternoon light before the park closes
items.note: Late-day light hits the laterite in warm tones — the best window for photos all day.

items.activity: Head back into town for a place to stay and dinner
items.note: Kamphaeng Phet town has an evening market along the Ping River — an easy place to stroll and find something to eat.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Drive to Sukhothai, cycle the temples

blocks.html: Leave Kamphaeng Phet early and take Highway 101 — about an hour-plus to Old Sukhothai. Lodging in the old town ranges from budget guesthouses to resorts with field views. Drop your bags, rent a bike at the park gate, and ride the walled zone, where the roads are smooth and there's plenty of shade — much better cycled than walked in the sun.

items.activity: Leave Kamphaeng Phet, drive Hwy 101 to Sukhothai
items.note: Through Phran Kratai and Khiri Mat, about 77 km, with gas stations and roadside cafes to stop at.

items.activity: Check in near the old town, drop your bags
items.note: Staying on the old-town side pays off — you can cycle straight into the park without driving in and out.

items.activity: Grab a bite before entering the park
items.note: Try Sukhothai noodles — thin rice noodles in a clear broth topped with yardlong beans and peanuts — or khao piap, a local dish that's hard to find outside the province.

items.activity: Rent a bike at the park gate, start at Wat Mahathat
items.note: The largest and most important temple in the walled zone. The highlight is the lotus-bud principal chedi, a signature of Sukhothai art.

items.activity: Cycle on to Wat Si Sawai and Wat Sa Si
items.note: Wat Si Sawai has three Lopburi-influenced prangs, while Wat Sa Si sits on an island in a pond, with a lovely chedi reflection when the water is still.

items.activity: Find a sunset spot in the park
items.note: Golden evening light on the old chedis is what people come to Sukhothai for. Cycle slowly and pick your angle before the light goes.

items.activity: Return the bike, find dinner around the old town
items.note: If your visit lands on a walking-street night, there's food and craft stalls to wander, with a nice atmosphere.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Mop up the remaining temples before heading home

blocks.html: Save the last day for spots you didn't reach the day before, especially Wat Si Chum, just north of the city wall. It holds the huge Phra Achana Buddha inside a solid-walled mondop — one of the classic Sukhothai shots that many people make the trip for. If you have time to spare and want to keep going, Si Satchanalai sits another hour or so north, a sister park in the same World Heritage group.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Wat Si Chum + food before you go

items.activity: Enter the park early, head to Wat Si Chum
items.note: Go early while crowds are thin and you can shoot Phra Achana in the mondop in peace. Morning light comes through the door gap beautifully.

items.activity: Cycle or drive to the temples you still haven't seen
items.note: The northern zone also has Wat Phra Phai Luang and Wat Saphan Hin on a hill — pick them off at your own pace.
Sukhothai town has several old shops that make their own noodles and have been open for decades. Have a bowl before you leave.
If you want to keep going, Si Satchanalai is about an hour north — easy to turn this into a 4-day trip.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss in either city

items.name: Sukhothai noodles
items.blurb: Thin rice noodles in a clear, slightly sweet broth, topped with sliced yardlong beans, roasted peanuts and crispy pork rind, with red pork or minced pork. It's the dish people picture when they think of Sukhothai. In town, several original shops make their own noodles and have been open for decades.

items.name: Khao piap Sukhothai
items.blurb: Thin sheets of dough filled and folded, then served in broth. In the local dialect "piap" means folded over and over. It's hard to find outside Sukhothai, so don't miss it if you like genuine regional food.

items.name: Kamphaeng Phet chicken noodles
items.blurb: Shredded-chicken noodles in a well-rounded broth, a Kamphaeng Phet town specialty. You'll find it at the old shops around town — a good breakfast before tackling the park.

items.name: Kamphaeng Phet egg bananas
items.blurb: Small thin-skinned egg bananas with a sweet, fragrant flavor — the province's signature. Eat them fresh, or take home candied or fried versions as a gift.

items.name: Ping riverside evening market, Kamphaeng Phet
items.blurb: A food market along the Ping River in town. A pleasant evening stroll to find local savory and sweet dishes, easygoing atmosphere and local prices.

blocks.text: Tips to make the trip smoother

items: Go early or late afternoon — midday sun is strong and hot in both cities. Duck into the shade for lunch around noon, then head back out as the light softens.
Stay on the old-town side of Sukhothai — it saves driving time, lets you cycle straight into the park, and keeps you near the sunset spots.
Carry small cash — zone-by-zone entry and bike rental are cash only, and many local shops still don't take transfers.
Hat, water, sunscreen — the ruins are open ground with little shade, so keep water on you.

items.name: Going without a car
items.blurb: You can take a bus or van between the two cities, but inside the parks you'll rely on a bike or tram, so build in extra time.

items.name: Want a longer trip
items.blurb: Add a day for Si Satchanalai to complete all three World Heritage towns in one trip, bumping it to 4 days.

faq.q: How far apart are Kamphaeng Phet and Sukhothai, and is it worth visiting both together?
faq.a: They're about 77 km apart by car, roughly 1 hour 15 minutes along Highway 101. Both are part of the same World Heritage group, so combining them into a 3-day trip is well worth it — you get both historical parks in a single journey.

faq.q: How much is entry to the two historical parks?
faq.a: Kamphaeng Phet is around 10 THB per zone for Thais and 30 THB for foreigners, while Sukhothai is around 20 THB per zone for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners. Both charge by zone. Bike rental adds about 20–30 THB for the day. Prices can change, so double-check on site.

faq.q: Should you cycle or walk the parks?
faq.a: Sukhothai's walled zone is great for cycling — smooth roads, plenty of shade, with bikes for rent at the park gate. In Kamphaeng Phet the temples are spread out: the inner-city zone is walkable, but you'll want to drive between temples in the Aranyik zone.

faq.q: What time of day looks best?
faq.a: Early morning and late afternoon near sunset, when golden light on the chedis and laterite looks its best. Midday is strong and hot, so duck into the shade for lunch around noon.

faq.q: If I have time to spare, where should I go next?
faq.a: Si Satchanalai is about an hour north of Old Sukhothai, a sister historical park in the same World Heritage group. Extend to a 4-day trip to cover all three towns.
